rationale: The Latin anchors *corruere* ("to collapse, fall down") and *muri illico corruerunt* ("the walls immediately fell/collapsed") point strongly to a sudden loss of upright position or structural collapse, matching fall.v.23 ("lose an upright position suddenly"). The additional Latin *cum fragore dissilire* ("burst apart with a crash") and *rumpi/frangi* ("to break/burst") confirm the violent, physical nature of the fall, consistent with BERSTAN's core sense of bursting/collapsing rather than any metaphorical or gradual descent.
